plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and lose when it wouldn't be profitable. With no prior history in this single-round game, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a weakly dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay less than my value when I do win. There's no strategic advantage to bidding above or below my true value of $18.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because if I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid below my value, I risk losing an auction I could have profitably won. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, my own bid only affects whether I win, not what I pay (given I win). Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $21.
